classification: Proposed alternative-history changes. Numerical cases are planning checks, not external historical measurements or fabricated lab evidence.

16 Kbit DRAM electrical interface and qualification
wafer, electrical and assembly yield denominators
reliability, test coverage and grade release

criteria.details: One physical line owns equipment and configurations; recipes reference it. Technologies own methods, assumptions own planning cases, processes own actions, events own dated accepted results. Three recruitment events become dated steps. The existing stepper process is unchanged. Generic capacity discussion retains only work outside this early-memory case.

1975 pilot and early DRAM/yield hiring; September 1976 initial ROM/1 Kbit SRAM; March 1977 4 Kbit SRAM; September 1977 16 Kbit DRAM; December 1977 four-tool provisioning; March 1978 sustained acceptance; May 1978 inventory and integration; June 5 launch. Released-product inventory cohorts begin before the March capacity gate, respecting up to 45+14 days elapsed production time. Six major events have single process ownership and dates within their owning periods.

criteria.result: pass as a demanding, funded alternative-history programme with explicit acceptance gates
criteria.details: Use conservative 190 candidate DRAM die per 75 mm wafer rather than the earlier illustrative 200. At 90% wafer completion, 60% accepted electrical yield and 95% assembly/final yield, 6,000 starts yield 584,820 accepted DRAMs, exceeding the 575,000 gate. SRAM capacity is separately checked. No repair or later stepper advantage is credited. Physical tool counts alone do not prove full-route throughput; the gate requires actual route loading, mask maps, lot evidence and additional test equipment if necessary.

Preserves finance forecast+5% headroom exactly once, secret-facility design-only role, existing six subprocesses, later 1979 stepper/64 Kbit and 1980 ERAv1 dates, generic external DRAM and unrelated records. No prices, invented customer agreements or sales actuals. RAM-card first commercial date remains unresolved. Memory acceptance does not claim all custom chips or complete-system production readiness.

further_work_not_silently_resolved: Capacity and cost modelling for later products and factories.
Detailed supplier selection, executed licences, assembly reservations and grade drawings belong to the named procurement/qualification actions; no external documentary proof is fabricated.
The RAM-card first public offering date remains an existing separate review issue.
Custom logic and complete-system manufacturing acceptance are outside the memory-only gate.
The 20,000-computer case needs additional DRAM and SRAM/assembly/test capacity; the 12,000-DRAM-start option is not installed capacity.
